vc-van.title: Miami Vice City Small-Group Tour
vc-van.desc: Our signature tour, by day or by night. Take the daytime run, or the sunset + night departure that starts at golden hour and ends when the neon switches on. Eight stops in one loop: the Ocean Drive neon, the Venetian Causeway, downtown, the Wynwood murals, Little Haiti, Little Havana and the Brickell skyline.

vc-car.title: Private Classic Convertible Tour
vc-car.desc: The most cinematic way to see it. Just your crew in a top-down vintage convertible with a driver-guide who knows every camera angle. Same stops as the signature tour, at your pace.
incl: Golden-hour photo stop on the causeway

vc-jeep.title: Private Jeep Convertible Tour
vc-jeep.desc: Roof off, wind in. Your crew in an open-top Jeep with a driver-guide, running the full Miami loop from the Ocean Drive neon up to the Brickell skyline.

vc-boat.title: Miami Vice City by Boat
vc-boat.desc: Our Millionaire’s Row cruise. Out of Bayside past PortMiami, Fisher Island and the Miami Beach Marina megayachts, then the celebrity mansions of Star, Palm and Hibiscus Islands and the Venetian Islands, ending with a golden-hour hold on the skyline.
good: Pairs well with the city tour

airboat.title: Grasslands Airboat
airboat.desc: Leave the neon behind for the real Everglades. Round-trip shuttle from Miami, then an airboat run through the sawgrass with a wildlife guide who knows where the gators sit. Add an alligator farm, or stay for a glow-in-the-dark ATV ride after sunset.
incl: Round-trip shuttle with pickup across greater Miami
good: A half day outside the city

keys.title: Leonida Keys Road Trip
keys.desc: The island road from the game, driven for real. The Overseas Highway through Key Largo and Islamorada to the Seven Mile Bridge, with beach time and a seafood lunch stop on the way.
incl: Beach time at a state park

pass.title: Leonida City Pass
pass.desc: Three tours on one pass: the Miami Vice City small-group tour, the boat tour and the Grasslands Airboat, booked on your own schedule. $237 of tours for $199.

vicecity.name: Miami Vice City
vicecity.blurb: Neon hotels, glass towers, murals and the bay. This is the city behind the game, and you can drive it in a small group, go private, or take it from the water.

grassrivers.name: Grasslands
grassrivers.blurb: Sawgrass to the horizon, airboats, gators and still water. The real Everglades, an hour from Miami.

keys.name: Leonida Keys
keys.blurb: Island roads, turquoise water and bridges that run to the horizon. A full-day road trip down the Keys.

ambrosia.name: Lake Okeechobee
ambrosia.blurb: Sugar country, flat roads that shimmer in the heat, and small-town stops. We’re scouting this route for 2027.

LAND.name: Ocean Drive
LAND.p: Start on Ocean Drive, where pastel Art Deco hotels, hand-painted neon and the Clevelander corner light up the night. Stand where the first trailer opened, then watch the strip come alive.
LAND.np: We finish here after dark, when the whole strip glows pink and blue.

LAND.name: Lummus Park Beach
LAND.p: Candy-striped lifeguard towers, white sand and Atlantic surf. The crew photo stop: everyone lines up by the tower, and everyone sends it to someone.
LAND.np: Golden-hour light on the lifeguard towers. The best crew photo of the night, every time.

LAND.name: Venetian Causeway
LAND.p: Cross the bay on the old Venetian Causeway, the skyline climbing ahead of you. Eyes out of the window for this one.

LAND.name: Downtown & Biscayne Blvd
LAND.p: The waterfront arena, a crown of changing light on the tallest tower, and the 24-hour superclub straight out of the second trailer.
LAND.np: Light trails down Biscayne Boulevard and tower crowns changing color. Downtown at its loudest.

LAND.name: Wynwood
LAND.p: A 25-minute walk through Wynwood’s murals, galleries and warehouse streets. The walls change every month, so no two crews ever get the same backdrop.
LAND.np: The murals under the streetlights, with the bars and music just starting up.

LAND.name: Little Haiti
LAND.p: Bright murals, loud color and patties from the counter at the cultural complex. The stop nobody expects to love most.

LAND.name: Little Havana
LAND.p: Cafecito and a pastelito at a ventanita, then dominoes at Máximo Gómez Park. Slow down here: this is the part of Miami you will still be talking about on the flight home.

LAND.name: Brickell
LAND.np: Glass towers lit up against a dark sky, then back over the MacArthur Causeway past the lit cruise ships to the neon of Ocean Drive.
LAND.p: Glass towers stacked to the sky in Brickell, then back over the MacArthur Causeway past the cruise ships at PortMiami and home to the neon on Ocean Drive.

WATER.name: Bayside Marina
WATER.p: Board under the downtown towers, with the arena and the waterfront right behind you.

WATER.name: PortMiami
WATER.p: Cruise past the giant cruise ships and cargo cranes of the world’s busiest cruise port.

WATER.name: Fisher Island
WATER.p: The island with no road, reachable only by boat or ferry, and home to some of the most expensive real estate in the US.

WATER.name: Miami Beach Marina
WATER.p: Superyachts lined up at the south end of Miami Beach, near South Pointe.

WATER.name: Star Island
WATER.p: The heart of Millionaire’s Row: celebrity mansions with private docks, one after another.

WATER.name: Palm & Hibiscus Islands
WATER.p: Palm-lined estates along the MacArthur Causeway, including the island where Al Capone once owned a waterfront house.

WATER.name: Venetian Islands
WATER.p: Weave between the islands and under the old drawbridge causeway.

WATER.name: Downtown & Brickell skyline
WATER.p: Engines off mid-bay for the golden-hour skyline shot, then back to Bayside.
